principles: Never silently weaken a signed gate: any downgrade keyed on a field of a signed record requires that field to be inside the signature.
Downgrade to a mandatory loud advisory, never to 'fresh', and never rebind the stored hash — preserve audit history.
Story-ownership of what was attested (storyFilesHash), not signed-ness, is the dividing line for the drift advisory.
Keep each DONE sub-gate's intent: frozen-ref integrity (A) and behavioral re-run (B) stay strict; only the diff-attestation freshness (C) relaxes.
drivers: Soundness of the signed delivery-check attestation (a wrong relaxation undermines the last gate before merge).
The recurring re-sign friction: unrelated main merges re-stale a byte-identical reviewed diff (observed 3x in B-70e4).
Consistency with the existing storyFilesHash secondary-freshness spec and its adopted bindings.

options.name: Downgrade Gate C with a signed storyFilesHash guard
pros: Consistent with the existing storyFilesHash advisory model
Story-owned changes and legacy-missing still hard-reject
Gate B still re-runs the suite, backstopping behavioral drift
cons: Touches the signature payload (must keep legacy recompute byte-identical)
Requires re-fixturing the all-on-main smoke to a story-branch topology

options.name: Keep Gate C strict (no change)
pros: Zero soundness risk to the signed gate
cons: Does not fix the friction — every unrelated merge still forces a reviewer re-sign of the same diff

options.name: Downgrade Gate C keyed on an UNSIGNED storyFilesHash
cons: Forgeable bypass: an editor can set storyFilesHash to match current and force the relaxation — converts the strongest signed gate into a bypass. Rejected.

chosen: Downgrade Gate C with a signed storyFilesHash guard
rationale: Locked by an adversarial design panel and the user's soundness call: downgrade only the signed delivery-check (Gate C) with storyFilesHash folded into the signature; keep Gate B re-running (cheap genuine behavioral re-verification that backstops the advisory) and Gate A strict (frozen-ref integrity). The unsigned-key option is a forgeable bypass and was rejected.

preMortem.trigger: storyFilesHash is stored but NOT folded into signDeliveryCheck/recomputeDeliveryCheckHash
preMortem.consequence: An editor sets storyFilesHash to match current and forces the advisory on a stale gate — the strongest signed gate becomes a bypass
preMortem.mitigation: Fold storyFilesHash into the signature payload; add a forged-storyFilesHash test asserting _hash breaks (delivery_check_tampered)

preMortem.trigger: An unrelated main merge changes a shared/transitive helper that alters real-machine test behavior while story-owned files are byte-identical
preMortem.consequence: The advisory accepts a delivery-check whose behavioral claim may no longer hold
preMortem.mitigation: Advisory is loud and mandatory (never 'fresh'); Gate B (done-required suite) stays strict and re-runs the full build+test on the merged tree, catching behavioral breakage

preMortem.trigger: The existing smoke fixture keeps HEAD on main, so currentStoryFilesHash is the empty-set constant and matches after ANY drift
preMortem.consequence: The smoke would assert a downgrade for changes that should be story-owned, masking a real mismatch path
preMortem.mitigation: Re-fixture to a story-branch topology (HEAD ahead of main); add explicit story-owned-change -> stale and legacy-missing -> strict cases

preMortem.trigger: A future change wires storyFilesHash into checkCompletedEvidenceSnapshotFreshness by analogy
preMortem.consequence: Softens a frozen-ref tamper detector into a soft warning for forge/rewrite mismatches
preMortem.mitigation: Add an explicit keep-strict code comment at done-oracle.ts:140 and a spec note that Gate A is excluded because it is a frozen-ref integrity check
